- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.3) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior period), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +5% above prior peak or use 3-period moving average.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.7) and price is trending up, model frequently overcorrects; apply downward bias of 1–3% to avoid overbought bias.
- When sentiment swings sharply (e.g., from 0.0 to 1.0), model reacts too quickly; delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 periods or use sentiment-weighted smoothing.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is >10% above 30-day moving average, reduce by 1–3% unless sentiment supports continuation.
- If sentiment is negative and price is falling, model often underestimates; add 1–3% upward bias to avoid premature bottoming.
